newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cultus up on Otway, exploration hopes.
newsitem.headline: Cultus up on Otway, exploration hopes.

text.p: Shares in junior oil and gas producer Cultus Petroleum Ltd pushed higher on Monday on positive sentiment over prospects in Victoria's Otway Basin and the possibility of new exploration permits, analysts said.
Cultus, which has risen sharply in recent months, was up 4.5 cents to A$3.00 at 12.00 p.m. (0200 GMT).
A Sydney-based analyst said Cultus was continuing to gain from positive sentiment surrounding the Otway Basin, following the announcement last week of the discovery of a new gas field.
Another said investors were hoping the company would be granted new exploration permits near its existing Cornea interests in the Browse Basin offshore Western Australia.
Cultus's share price rose sharply in February after a consortium in which Cultus has a 25 percent stake discovered oil in Browse Basin permit WA-241-P.
The permit is operated by Royal Dutch/Shell unit Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd, which holds 50 percent, while Chevron Corp unit Chevron Asiatic Ltd has 25 percent.
A Cultus operated consortium was also last week offered an exploration block in the Timor Sea, north of Australia, in the latest release of petroleum exploration permits.
